sentences.text: 4 Bengaluru
. Respondent No.2 is the complainant.
2. The case of the complainant is that he supplied timber to accused No.1 and he was introduced to accused No.1 by accused No.2.
However, accused No.1 did not pay him the necessary consideration.

3. Based on the complaint of the complainant, the State has filed a police report alleging that the accused are guilty of the offence under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short, 'the IPC').
4.

The case of accused No.2 is that he only introduced accused No.1 to the complainant and they NC:
2025:KHC:50412 HC-KAR might have transacted amongst themselves and without any reason, false allegations have been made against him.
5.
The case of accused No.1 is that he admits the fact that he received the necessary timber.
But it is submitted that the timber was of inferior quality and hence, the same has been returned.
It is also fairly submitted that the complainant filed a civil suit against accused No.1, which has been decreed in favour of the complainant.
6. The learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2 is absent.
7. The learned High Court Government Pleader, upon instructions, submits that there are no materials against accused No.2 and the transaction is only between accused No.1 and the complainant.
It is further submitted that accused No.1 relies upon an e-way bill as evidence to show that he has sent back the timber to the complainant.
NC: 2025:KHC:50412 HC-KAR
However, the investigation has revealed that the said e- way bill is a bogus e-way bill.
8. Based on the aforementioned submissions of the respective counsel and the materials placed on record, it becomes clear that there is no case against accused No.2.

However, with regard to accused No.1, whether he has sent back the timber or not is a matter of trial, more so, in the light of the decision of the trial Court passing a decree in favour of the complainant directing accused No.1 to pay him certain amounts.

Hence, the following:
ORDER i. Crl.P.No.4363/2023 is hereby allowed and consequently, the proceedings in C.C.No.55550/2022, pending on the file of the X Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru, insofar as it relates to accused No.2 (petitioner in Crl.P.No.4363/2023) is quashed.
